children: Infragreen Group
is an Australia-based diversified infrastructure investor and operator focused on sustainable assets across Australia and New Zealand.
With an established portfolio spanning recycling, waste recovery, and energy transition, the company operates across key thematic sectors driven by decarbonisation and resource efficiency mandates.
Infragreen operates as an infrastructure platform designed to acquire, hold, and scale businesses operating within green infrastructure and resource recovery.

Led by chief executive officer and managing director Declan Sherman and Non-executive chair Lindsay Ward, the group targets mid-market assets positioned to benefit from structural shifts towards circular economy initiatives and clean energy generation.
Portfolio and Projects

Infragreen's portfolio is structured into core operational divisions covering regulated and hazardous waste processing, metal recycling, solar and clean energy solutions for new residential houses, and peaking energy infrastructure.
The company’s business model is built around four primary operating platforms:
Pure Environmental:
Focuses on regulated waste recycling and resource recovery services.
Minemet:
A vertically integrated recycling entity that collects, processes, and exports ferrous and non-ferrous metals across domestic and international markets.
Energybuild:
An installer of solar and clean energy solutions catering to high volume residential homebuilders.
Merredin Energy:
Operates peaking power infrastructure designed to provide grid support as renewable generation expands, and dispatchable electricity during peak periods.
Financial Context
In its FY2026 financial disclosures, Infragreen reported a net profit after tax of A7.6 million, with total equity standing at A149.23 million.
During the reporting period, the company paid a fully franked interim dividend of 0.50 cents per share and announced a final dividend of 0.50 cents per share.

The board has also maintained an active on-market share buy-back program of up to A$10 million, while executing an ongoing strategic review of its portfolio to assess capital allocation and asset performance across its operating divisions.
Energy Transition and Resource Security
The broader macroeconomic environment for green infrastructure and critical materials continues to be defined by global energy transition policy and supply chain security.
Circular Economy & Scrap Metals:
Increased industrial demand for recycled non-ferrous metals—such as copper and aluminium—reflects global mandates to reduce primary smelting emissions and improve material reuse.
Grid Stabilization & Renewable Integration:
The build-out of solar assets and variable renewable power generation requires accompanying fast-start peaking energy infrastructure to ensure grid reliability during demand spikes.
Critical Minerals Awareness:

Heightened focus on critical raw materials and battery supply chains has elevated domestic interest in resource efficiency, recycling technologies, and essential energy transition inputs across Australasia.
Key Considerations
Infragreen enters the current period with a diversified exposure to sustainable infrastructure services, underpinned by an active strategic review and capital management activities.

Future performance across the group will depend on key external and internal variables, including regional power prices, industrial activity levels, waste processing volumes, regulatory policy frameworks, and execution of its capital management strategies.

title: Infragreen Positions Portfolio for Clean Energy and Circular Economy Demand
